Read the literature evidence table, filtered by species and variable

Source: R/literature.R
knw_literature_read.Rd

One row per value a source gives for a habitat variable: species, life stage, life-history form, variable, the model parameter it bears on (parameter, e.g. spawn_gradient_max), bound, value, unit, metric, kind, region, citation key, page and a verbatim quote. value_min and value_max are numbers written as text, or MM-DD for timing, where a range with value_min > value_max crosses 1 January. Gradient is in percent, as sources write it; a model that stores gradient as a proportion divides by 100. cited_source names the original study when the quote is a secondary citation of it. model_id links a row to the intrinsic-potential model it states a threshold of, as described in the registry read by knw_ip_read(); it is blank for a row that is not a model's parameter.

Usage

knw_literature_read(path, species_code = NULL, variable = NULL)

Arguments

path

character(1) path to the evidence CSV.

species_code

character species codes to keep, or NULL for all.

variable

character variables to keep (see knw_literature_vocab()), or NULL for all.

Value

A tibble with the twenty columns, all character.

Details

The unit must fit the variable (percent for gradient, a width unit for channel width, and so on) and a bound must sit on its value: min on value_min, max on value_max, range on both. A text quote is at least 20 characters, so that a check against the PDF can tell it apart from noise. A temperature, air_temperature, degree_days, instream_flow or fish_length value needs a metric that fits its variable, and a none row may name the metric it searched for; every other row leaves metric blank. A cited degree_days row needs a note, which gives the base temperature.

A qual row is a statement with no value. A row of kind none records a search that found no value: it carries a note saying what was searched and no value, key or quote. Its bound and metric, when given, name what was searched for (an upper limit, a degree-day total to emergence). Every other row needs a citation_key and a quote. A row with a value needs a unit.

The table is validated before filtering, so a bad row anywhere in the file is an error whichever species is asked for. A requested species or variable absent from the table is a warning, so a typo does not read as "no evidence".

Examples

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(data.frame(
  species_code = "BT", life_stage = "spawning", life_history_form = "migratory",
  variable = "channel_width", parameter = "spawn_channel_width_min", bound = "min",
  value_min = "2", value_max = NA, unit = "m wetted", metric = NA, kind = "expert",
  region = "Parsnip, BC", citation_key = "key_a", page = "22",
  quote = "No streams of <2 m wetted width were surveyed", quote_source = "text",
  scale = "reach", cited_source = NA, note = NA, model_id = NA
), path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
knw_literature_read(path, species_code = "BT", variable = "channel_width")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 20
#>   species_code life_stage life_history_form variable   parameter bound value_min
#>   <chr>        <chr>      <chr>             <chr>      <chr>     <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 BT           spawning   migratory         channel_w… spawn_ch… min   2        
#> # ℹ 13 more variables: value_max <chr>, unit <chr>, metric <chr>, kind <chr>,
#> #   region <chr>, citation_key <chr>, page <chr>, quote <chr>,
#> #   quote_source <chr>, scale <chr>, cited_source <chr>, note <chr>,
#> #   model_id <chr>
